title: Fence Painting & Staining in Trenton, FL
description: Fence painting and staining in Trenton FL for wood and vinyl fences: cleaning, board repair, tannin-blocking primer, and stain or paint chosen for the run.
h1: Fence Painting and Staining in Trenton, FL
heroIntro: From a short privacy fence downtown to a long run along a homestead, we clean, repair, and coat Trenton fences so they stop graying and splitting.

questions: Should I paint or stain my wood fence?
Can a vinyl fence be painted?
Why does my fence turn black at the bottom?

sections.h2: Fences wear from the ground up
body: A fence lives in the worst spot on the property. Its posts sit in wet soil, sprinklers soak the lower boards, and both faces take full sun. That is why fences in Trenton usually turn black and fuzzy at the bottom while the tops go silver and split. Fence painting in Trenton FL starts by killing the mildew and algae at the base, not by covering it.
On rural homesteads where a fence line runs a long distance, we walk the whole length during the estimate and mark loose pickets, leaning sections, and boards that need replacing.

sections.h2: Stain or paint: how we decide
body: For most wood fences we recommend a penetrating stain. It soaks in, does not peel, and is simpler to refresh later. Paint makes sense when you want a solid color or are matching the house, and then the bare wood gets a primer that blocks tannin bleed so brown streaks do not come through. Vinyl fences can be cleaned and coated with a product suited to vinyl, which we name on the estimate.
bullets: Replace or re-fasten loose and damaged boards
Spot-prime bare and tannin-heavy wood when painting
Stain or paint both faces, posts, and caps
Protect plantings and rinse landscaping before we leave

body: Most fence jobs fit into a short stretch of dry days. October through May is the steadiest window; in summer we stain in the mornings before storms build. Many owners pair a fence with a Trenton deck refinish so all exposed wood is on the same maintenance cycle.

Fence projects vary more than most. The estimate depends on total length and height, whether one or both faces are coated, the condition of the boards, and whether you choose stain or paint. Picket and shadowbox styles have more edges than flat privacy panels, which adds time. Gates, posts, and post caps are listed separately so you can include them or not. Like every job, nothing is added later without your written approval.
See our main deck and fence staining page, our page on exterior cleaning in Trenton, the Trenton painter hub, and our guide to treating a sun-damaged wood fence.

faqs.q: Do you stain both sides of the fence?
faqs.a: We can. The estimate lists which faces, posts, and caps are included, so you know exactly what is covered.

faqs.q: My fence is gray and rough. Can it be saved?
faqs.a: Often yes. Washing and sanding can bring weathered wood back, and boards that are too far gone are replaced before staining.

faqs.q: Can you paint a vinyl fence?
faqs.a: Yes, with cleaning and a coating made for vinyl. We will tell you during the walkthrough if a color change is practical.

faqs.q: Will stain get on my plants and grass?
faqs.a: We cover and protect plantings along the fence line and rinse landscaping before we leave each day.
